evidence: The acquire() docstring said it 'opens the session as well as fetching' while the body only called _install; the agent admits 'I split _install and _open after writing that docstring and did not go back', and 4477a99 makes acquire call _open and adds a test that a non-model .onnx fails the bake.
guidance_note: When splitting a helper in two, re-read every docstring on the callers that described the pre-split behaviour and check each claim against the new call graph.

evidence: The round-0 hunk shows _fetch_timeless_export renaming .partial into place with no size check and no finally-unlink, unlike kokoro._fetch; 4477a99 deletes it and routes through kokoro._fetch with a URL parameter.
guidance_note: Before hand-writing download/verify/rename logic in a test fixture, call the production function that already does it, widening its signature if needed.

evidence: installed_assets acquired both engines plus the timeless export, so Piper-only modules required Kokoro assets and espeak-ng; 4477a99 splits into piper_installed/kokoro_installed/kokoro_timeless_installed and the agent confirmed via --setup-plan.
guidance_note: When replacing a per-engine skip marker with a provisioning fixture, give each engine its own fixture so a module only pays for the engine it exercises.

evidence: Duplicate of F2 on the same lines (missing empty-body guard and cleanup); fixed by the same deletion in 4477a99 rather than by copying the guard.

subject(request, installed_assets) gated the synthetic DeclaredEngine params on downloads; instead of per-param indirection, 4477a99 removes the fixture from subject and has piper_engine/kokoro_engine open with allow_download=True, which removes the coupling more simply.
guidance_note: When a parametrized fixture mixes fake and real subjects, put asset provisioning inside the real subjects' factories, not on the shared fixture.

evidence: test_api.py is Piper-only yet used usefixtures('installed_assets'); 4477a99 switches it to piper_installed.
The module docstring still said 'Skipped rather than mocked when no model is installed' after the skip marker was removed in the same diff; 4477a99 rewrites it to say the voice is fetched.
guidance_note: When removing a mechanism such as a skip marker, grep the touched modules' docstrings for the words describing it (skip, skipped) before committing.

evidence: Third duplicate of F2 (unguarded rename into the shared models cache); resolved by the same deletion in 4477a99.

It is true that the command substitution's status is head's, so an empty glob is not caught by that command. But the claim that 'ln -s "" ...' then succeeds is overstated: Linux symlink(2) rejects an empty target with ENOENT, so the build would most likely fail, just with an unclear error. The explicit test -n in 4477a99 is still the clearer assertion.
guidance_note: When a shell step is meant to prove a dependency exists, make the existence check its own command rather than relying on a later command happening to fail.

evidence: 0.77/0.03 is about 25.7, not twenty. The reviewer named three locations (README, engines.py, kokoro.py module docstring), but the agent's plan says 'Fixing both places you name' and 4477a99 only touches README and engines.py, which leaves kokoro.py for F14/F16/F17/F19.
guidance_note: When a finding lists every place a phrase appears, grep the repo for the phrase itself and fix every hit, rather than working from the finding's anchor or a remembered subset.

evidence: numpy.load on the .npz pack was never closed; 4477a99 wraps it in a with-block and reads the names inside it, so both the success and the ValueError paths close the handle.

The README explained that the bundled espeak library aborts but never told a non-Docker reader to set PHONEMIZER_ESPEAK_LIBRARY. 4477a99 adds the instruction but lists only two paths, even though the reviewer pointed at conftest's candidate list. That gap became F21.
guidance_note: When documenting a value the code already enumerates, such as conftest's library candidates, copy the code's full list into the doc instead of a sample.

evidence: 4477a99 (F3's fix) renamed installed_assets into three per-engine fixtures. The conftest module docstring still says '`DeclaredEngine` and `installed_assets` are here', which names a symbol that fix deleted.
guidance_note: After renaming or splitting a symbol, grep the whole repo for the old name, including docstrings, before pushing the fix.

evidence: 4477a99 corrected 'twenty' to 'twenty-five' in README and engines.py only, and the kokoro.py header still said 'roughly twenty times'. The agent dropped the derived multiplier where the raw RTFs sit on the same line, which removes a drift-prone copy.
guidance_note: When fixing a derived number restated in several files, grep for every copy and decide once whether each copy should exist at all.

evidence: Duplicate of F13: the conftest docstring names installed_assets, which F3's fix in 4477a99 split away; fixed in b212df5.
Duplicate of F14: the kokoro.py header copy that F10's fix skipped, resolved in 2d36b6b by removing the multiplier.
Duplicate of F14. The reviewer notes the original F10 finding 'explicitly named' kokoro.py, and that file was skipped.

The flag is a false positive for causation: the _RELEASE comment ('The older release remains a working choice') shipped in the original commit and 4477a99 did not touch it. The claim is false because _install builds f'{_RELEASE}/{model}' from a pinned release. Of the reviewer's two options, the agent took 'correct this comment'.
guidance_note: When a comment says an option is available to operators, trace the config path that reaches it before writing the claim.

evidence: Fourth duplicate of F14 on the kokoro.py header copy F10's fix missed; resolved in 2d36b6b.

F3's fix in 4477a99 rewrote test_kokoro.py's pytestmark from installed_assets to kokoro_installed, leaving a module-wide asset gate on pure config-parse and _pcm tests. That is the same coupling F3 removed between modules. The agent dropped the mark in b212df5 and showed the -k boolean plan has no kokoro fixture.
guidance_note: When narrowing a fixture's reach for composability, apply the same test inside each module: a module-level usefixtures is only right if every test in that module needs it.

evidence: The README block that 4477a99 added for F12 lists only the macOS-homebrew and x86_64 Linux paths, while _use_a_working_espeak() knows four, including aarch64. F12 had pointed at 'the same candidates conftest.py checks'. ee996d4 lists all four.
guidance_note: When a finding says to mirror a list the code already holds, open that list and copy every entry instead of writing the common cases.

evidence: Duplicate of F20: the module-level kokoro_installed mark that F3's fix rewrote but did not remove; fixed in b212df5.

_SAMPLE_RATE = 24000 shipped in the original commit, so 4477a99 did not cause this. Reading the rate from create()'s tuple would force eager synthesis because speak returns Speech with an unstarted generator, which the packet's code shows. The packet cannot confirm the agent's claim that kokoro_onnx returns a module constant, but importing the library's SAMPLE_RATE removes the duplicate either way.
guidance_note: When a module restates a library's constant, import the library's symbol instead of copying its value.

evidence: _VOICE_LANGUAGES only reached _describe(), so codes for the default bf_emma/bm_george voices were never passed to espeak. The table was in the original commit, so the flag is a false positive for causation. b212df5 asserts all nine codes against EspeakBackend.supported_languages() and adds a real bf_emma speak().
guidance_note: When adding a mapping of external-system codes, add one test that hands each value to the real external system rather than only copying it into labels.

evidence: The Voice licensing section discussed only Piper after a second engine with 54 voices was added. That is an original-PR omission the round-0 reviewer missed, not fix-caused. ee996d4 states Kokoro's Apache-2.0 model licence and the MIT wrapper licence.
guidance_note: When adding a second implementation behind a seam, grep the README for every section that names the first one, such as licensing and defaults, and extend each.

narrative: Round 0 raised twelve real findings (several triplicated) against a large new-engine PR, and the agent accepted all of them, mostly with sound fixes. Nine of round 1's thirteen findings came from 4477a99's own fixes: the twenty-to-twenty-five correction skipped the kokoro.py copy the reviewer had named, the installed_assets split left a stale docstring and a module-wide gate in test_kokoro.py, and the espeak README fix listed two of four known paths. Round 1 would have run anyway because F18, F23, F24 and F25 were independent, so no round was strictly avoidable, but the fix-caused findings made up most of its volume.
guidance_observations: The agent fixed 'both places you name' when the reviewer had named three, so the fix worked from a paraphrase instead of re-reading the finding text.
Each rename or split in the fix commit (installed_assets) needed a repo-wide grep for the old name, and none was done before pushing.
Several round-0 findings were filed three times against the same lines, and the agent handled the duplicates efficiently with one fix and cross-referenced replies.

evidence: Docker's reference says variable substitution in RUN is done by the command shell, not the builder, and a double-quoted parameter expansion is not re-parsed. The agent showed the payload became one argv element and touched nothing, and a bad value makes uv reject an undeclared extra. Rejecting a hardcoded case list of engines rightly avoids a second copy of ENGINES.

The engines.py checklist still named test_encoding._ENGINE_LIBRARIES after the PR moved it to conftest.ENGINE_LIBRARIES, and it omitted the new pyproject extra. 3fd1ee1 rewrites it to name both and to mark which item test_packaging.py enforces.
guidance_note: When moving a symbol that a 'how to add an engine' checklist names, grep for the old name and update the checklist in the same commit.

evidence: The PR moved piper-tts into an extra but left README's 'uv run main.py', so the documented first run would install no engine; the agent admits 'I updated the Tests section ... and left the Running-it section'. 3fd1ee1 updates the README and adds a test that README start commands name a registered extra. The agent's refusal to relabel ModuleNotFoundError as ConfigError is reasoned.
guidance_note: When making a dependency optional, run the README's literal quickstart commands in a clean environment before pushing.

narrative: There were three findings in round 0. One was a false injection premise, correctly rebutted with documentation and a reproduction, and the other two were real doc drifts caused by the original change. Both fixes went in a single commit, round 1 found nothing, and no finding traces to an earlier fix.
guidance_observations: The pushback on F1 tested the reviewer's mechanism directly by running the payload instead of arguing from authority, which is the right shape for a pushback.
Both accepted findings were docs left stale by the PR's own move or split; a grep for moved names and a run of the README commands before opening the PR would have prevented the round.

evidence: The tr/sed pipeline keeps leading indentation, so the anchored sed matches nothing on pretty-printed JSON and the counter silently restarts at .1. The agent reproduced 'OLD pipeline: [] / NEW pipeline: [1]' on the real registry, and 65c9567 switches to jq -r '.tags[]? // empty'.
guidance_note: When a step already depends on jq, parse every JSON body with jq rather than with text tools that assume a layout.

evidence: CLAUDE.md said a branch push surfaces 'a Dockerfile problem', but reachability only builds a synthetic busybox probe. 65c9567 narrows the claim, but it also adds advice to dispatch on a branch, which F5 then showed contradicts the 'only git push gitea master' sentence and moves :latest.
guidance_note: When adding operational advice to a policy doc, check it against every absolute claim in the same section and against what the workflow actually does on that trigger.

evidence: Duplicate of F1 on the same tr/sed parse; resolved by the same jq change in 65c9567.

The flag is a false positive for causation: body=$(mktemp) with no cleanup is already in the round-0 hunk, and 65c9567 changed only the parse line. The leak is real. 4e49555 installs trap 'rm -f "$body"' EXIT right after mktemp, which the reviewer offered and which covers the three exit 1 paths.
guidance_note: Every mktemp in a set -e script gets its trap on the next line, as the probe step in the same file already did.

evidence: 65c9567 (F2's fix) added 'dispatch the workflow on the branch; that is what the dispatch trigger is for', which contradicts the pre-existing 'only ... git push gitea master' line. Such a dispatch also really moved both :latest aliases. 4e49555 makes :latest master-only in the workflow, and run 5230 confirms a branch dispatch left :latest unchanged.
guidance_note: Before recommending a trigger in docs, read what the workflow publishes on that trigger, and make the workflow enforce any invariant the doc promises.

evidence: 4e49555 (F5's fix) made :latest master-only and rewrote the paragraphs above, but left 'each also tagged :latest' in the next paragraph of the same CLAUDE.md section. e6ee1b1 scopes it to master.
guidance_note: After changing a rule, grep the doc for every mention of the thing the rule governs (here ':latest') and re-scope each one.

evidence: The flag is a false positive for causation: the grep -q '=$' guard and its 'covers every label' comment are in the labels step, which 4e49555's diff does not touch. The premise holds because source= and build.run= end in literal text after their last variable. d4492bc moves to ${VAR:?} at interpolation, which the reviewer suggested, and the agent ran the empty-variable cases.
guidance_note: When writing a guard on composed output, test it against an input where the empty value sits mid-string, not only at the end.

narrative: Round 0 found a real silent-overwrite bug in tag parsing and an overclaim in CLAUDE.md. The doc fix for F2 added advice to dispatch on a branch, which contradicted the doc's own 'only master' claim and had in fact moved :latest. The agent fixed that structurally in the workflow (F5), but the rewrite left a third unqualified ':latest' sentence (F6). Rounds 1 and 2 each also held an independent finding (F4, F7), so no round was strictly avoidable, but the doc chain ran three rounds deep.
guidance_observations: Each doc fix in this PR was checked against the sentence being edited but not against the rest of the section, which is how F5 and F6 arose.
The agent repeatedly verified against the real runner and registry instead of reasoning, and that turned F1 and F5 from claims into measurements.

evidence: engine_name was new load-bearing state with no from_env assertion. 55c8e26 adds an engine_name == 'first' assertion and a second-entry test, and the agent mutated _prepare to return the first key to show the test catches it.
guidance_note: When adding a field that selects a file, test both the producer and the consumer that reads the file.

evidence: The FOREIGN_ID comment named elvenspeak/aliases.toml, which the PR deleted; 55c8e26 renames it to aliases/piper.toml.
guidance_note: When deleting a file, grep for its filename across tests and comments in the same commit.

evidence: F1's fix tested that from_env produces the right engine_name, but not that create_app passes it to the alias table. The existing substitution test only observes a fallback, which is the same outcome for the right, wrong or missing table. 8cf91f4 adds a decoy-table test that only the correct table passes.
guidance_note: When a finding says wrong state would 'silently load the wrong table', write the test at the point the table is read, with a decoy that makes a wrong load visible.

evidence: The flag is a false positive for causation: ARG PIPER_VOICES was set in 5c4d7dd, and 55c8e26 only touched tests. The agent agreed the drift is the live bug this PR fixes, then deferred the check to a ticket because no CI runs pytest yet. Local runs would still catch the drift, and a subset assertion is a strict part of the wider cross-engine check, so it would not need a rewrite later.
guidance_note: When a PR fixes a drift bug between two declarations, add the test that ties them together in the same PR rather than leaving the fix guarded only by a comment.

evidence: The flag is a false positive for causation: the DEFAULT_VOICE comment is from the original commit, and 8cf91f4 touched only test_api.py. The agent measured the files: high is about 114 MB and medium 63 MB, which sums to the Dockerfile's ~291 MB, so 'same price' was false. e993d17 states the real cost.
guidance_note: Before writing a size or cost claim in a comment, measure the specific artifact the claim is about rather than a neighbouring tier.

narrative: Round 0 found a missing test for the new engine_name field and a stale filename comment. F1's fix tested only the producer side, and round 1 asked for the consumer-side wiring test (F3), along with an independent request to tie the alias targets to the baked voices (F4), which the agent deferred to a ticket. Round 2's F5 was an original-PR comment whose size claim the agent then measured and corrected. Each later round also held an independent finding, so none was strictly avoidable.
guidance_observations: The agent mutation-checked each new test against the defect it targets, which made the F1 and F3 tests trustworthy.
Deferring F4 to a separate ticket left the PR's own drift bug guarded only by comments and a manual check at merge.

evidence: The PR is titled 'DO NOT MERGE' and the agent's 11:49 issue comment says it was closed unmerged after the gate refused it, two minutes before this 11:51 review. The risk that the always-failing file lands on master did not exist. The flag marks the PR's own deliberate content, not a fix. A one-line rejection would have closed the open thread, but leaving it cost nothing.

narrative: This was a throwaway PR to show that the new required pytest check blocks a red commit. It was closed unmerged by design, and the only finding, which warned the failing test could reach master, arrived after closure and had no live premise.
guidance_observations: Review ran on a PR whose title and state showed it would never merge, so the round produced only noise.
